messages:
maya: Noticed several restores failing this morning with KMS AccessDenied when trying to decrypt snapshots during customer recovery.

tom: Which customer / snapshots? any error excerpts?

maya: Tenant-77, snapshots snap-20260321-a and snap-20260321-b. Error seen in worker logs: "AccessDenied: user=arn:aws:iam::123456:role/backup-restorer cannot perform kms:Decrypt on key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/cmk-77abcd"

eli: That key was rotated last week to alias/backup-main. We ran an iam-slimdown job that tightened roles. Possible the restore role lost decrypt rights.

lina: @tom please pull CloudTrail KMS events 02:15-02:30 UTC and the IAM change history for role backup-restorer.

sec-bot: IAM change detected: pipeline infra/minor-iam-cleanup updated role backup-restorer at 2026-03-21T02:18:04Z. Removed broad kms:* and left only kms:Encrypt and kms:GenerateDataKey. (change id: iamc-20260321-44)

dena: So uploads were fine but restores broken. We need a fast remediation path and a safer long-term model. Thoughts?

oncall-ops: Immediate fix: temporarily add a scoped kms:Decrypt allow for the specific CMK ARN on backup-restorer role. Prefer inline for speed and then replace with CM (customer-managed) policy.

maya: Agreed. Also log the change reason and link to this thread. Notify the customer about delay and that we're working on a fix.

tom: Quick check: snapshot metadata table shows key_id = cmk-77abcd for the two failing snaps. No bulk mismatch.

eli: I'll push the emergency inline patch. Proposed policy JSON snippet (inline):

```
{
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt", "kms:GenerateDataKey"],
  "Resource": "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/cmk-77abcd"
}
```

sec-bot: Reminder: include justification and ticket ref in the change description. All inline fixes must be short-lived and tracked.

oncall-ops: Hotfix applied at 6123456900. Please attempt a restore validation.

lina: Re-ran restore flow: KMS Decrypt succeeded, restore completed. Logs:

```
2026-03-21T02:22:11Z KMS Decrypt arn:aws:kms:...cmk-77abcd Success principal backup-restorer
2026-03-21T02:22:17Z Restore pipeline completed for snap-20260321-a
```

dena: Hotfix works. Next: design a preventable workflow so role scoping doesn't break restore. I propose two changes: 1) adopt KMS Grants for ephemeral decrypt during restores, 2) maintain a central role-policy matrix that the iam-cleanup pipeline consults.

eli: For (1) I can prototype grant issuance from the restore controller: it calls KMS CreateGrant for the restore principal, uses the grant token in the restore request, and revokes or lets it expire after the job.

maya: That sounds promising. Grants are auditable and time-boxed. But we need fallback behavior if grant creation fails (e.g., a service policy with explicit decrypt on alias as a fallback path).

oncall-ops: Also important: ensure cross-account restores (some customers restore into their own AWS accounts) handle grant semantics; may require external principals and different grant patterns.

lina: Action items (assignments):
- eli: MR to remove inline hotfix and add least-privilege managed policy + add unit test in infra pipelines (ETA: 3h)
- tom: build a small tool to scan roles for missing kms:Decrypt where a restore-capable tag exists on service roles (ETA: 12h)
- dena: draft RFC for KMS grant-based restore workflow with failure modes, aliasing strategy, and rotation implications (ETA: 4d)
- maya: customer notification and short post-incident note (ETA: 1h)
- sec-bot: add CI gate to iam-cleanup pipeline to detect removal of kms:Decrypt from known restore roles; block if no compensating grant mechanism

eli: Also found a minor telemetry gap: our existing alerts aggregate restore failures but don't surface KMS AccessDenied specifics. Propose a new metric filter for CloudTrail events where eventName == "Decrypt" and errorCode == "AccessDenied" along with the resource key and job id.

sec-bot: Added alert suggestion to backlog: 'restore.kms.decrypt.access_denied' with severity P2.

dena: Other notes: run a one-off inventory across all tenants to find snapshots encrypted with deprecated or rotated keys that might lack grants in current policy matrix. We might need a migration plan.

maya: Good catch. tom, can you run an inventory query to list snapshots per key alias and mark tenants with mixed-key histories? Put results in the ticket.

oncall-ops: Quick operational guidance: when rotating CMKs, include a step to reconcile role policies and grants; add a pre-rotation smoke test that attempts a test decrypt of a staging snapshot.

eli: I'll add the smoke test to key rotation playbook. Also will prototype a library to request grants with automatic revoke on job completion.

lina: Longer term security preference: avoid inline role edits for hotfixes if possible. Use managed policies and a documented emergency procedure that creates temporary grants instead.

maya: Thanks team. I'll follow up with a brief postmortem and link the MR + RFC once created. Marking this thread for post-incident review with eng-sre and product-security. :white_check_mark:
